alert.gpu_hot.summary: A GPU is at or above the temperature where the dashboard warns, 85 degrees Celsius.
alert.gpu_hot.details: Cards slow themselves down when they get too hot, which cuts speed, and long periods of heat shorten their life. The warning appears on the dashboard and on the host page.
alert.gpu_hot.when_to_change: Check the fan speed and airflow, clean dust, lower the power limit, or reduce the load.
alert.gpu_hot.risks: Sustained heat leads to throttling and, in the worst case, to the card shutting itself down.
alert.gpu_hot.example: A card at 88 degrees during a long benchmark.

alert.host_ram_low.summary: The machine is running low on RAM that can be given to programs.
alert.host_ram_low.details: The console compares the RAM available (free plus cache the kernel can drop) with the total. Below 10% it warns. Below 5% it is critical. New engines may be ended by the kernel when this happens.
alert.host_ram_low.when_to_change: Stop an engine you do not need, turn off CPU offload or host caches, or add RAM. Check shared memory: it may be taking more than it seems.
alert.host_ram_low.risks: Critical means the kernel may end the biggest process, often an engine, and the machine may swap.
alert.host_ram_low.example: 20 GiB available on a 256 GiB machine is 8%: a warning.

alert.shmem_high.summary: Shared memory takes more than a quarter of the machine's RAM, and it cannot be given back.
alert.shmem_high.details: Tools count shared memory as cache, so it looks harmless, but the kernel cannot reclaim it. Multi-GPU engines are the usual cause. The RAM that is really available is lower than the free-memory figure suggests.
alert.shmem_high.when_to_change: Check which engines hold shared memory on the host page. Stopping one returns its share.
alert.shmem_high.risks: Starting another engine, or a download, may fail for lack of memory even though 'cache' looks large.
alert.shmem_high.example: 70 GiB of shared memory on a 256 GiB machine.

alert.swap_heavy.summary: More than half of the machine's swap is in use, so it is short of memory.
alert.swap_heavy.details: Swap is disk space used when RAM is full. Using most of it means programs are being pushed out of memory, and things that live in swap run very slowly.
alert.swap_heavy.when_to_change: Free memory: stop an engine, reduce offload, or add RAM. Look at the RAM figures to see which engine holds the memory.
alert.swap_heavy.risks: Engines whose memory is swapped out stall and replies take much longer.

alert.vram_full.summary: A GPU's memory is almost completely used.
alert.vram_full.details: There is no room left for another engine, and a spike in one engine's use can cause an out-of-memory error. It is normal for a card that holds one big engine, since engines reserve their share when they start, but it leaves nothing for anything else.
alert.vram_full.when_to_change: If the card should have room, find out what holds the memory on the host page. Stop an engine or lower its memory share.
alert.vram_full.risks: A new launch on this card will fail the memory check.
alert.vram_full.example: A card at 98% used by one engine.

check.api_key_blocks_metrics.summary: With an API key set the engine refuses its metrics page, so live metrics disappear.
check.api_key_blocks_metrics.details: llama-server protects its metrics endpoint with the same key as its API. The console does not send engine keys when it collects metrics, so the throughput and queue charts stay empty for this engine.
check.api_key_blocks_metrics.when_to_change: Leave the engine's own key unset: the console already sits in front of the engine and requires its own key.
check.api_key_blocks_metrics.risks: No live metrics for this engine; chat still works.
check.api_key_blocks_metrics.example: An api-key set on a llama.cpp engine that the console launched.

check.attention_backend_dc_blackwell.summary: The chosen attention backend is built for data-centre Blackwell cards (sm_100) and is unconfirmed on yours (sm_120).
check.attention_backend_dc_blackwell.details: Attention backends are compiled for particular GPU generations. This one targets data-centre Blackwell. Your card is a workstation or consumer Blackwell with compute capability 12.0, a different family, and the console has no confirmation that it works there.
check.attention_backend_dc_blackwell.when_to_change: Leave the backend on auto, or choose flashinfer or triton, which are known to run on these cards.
check.attention_backend_dc_blackwell.risks: A start-up failure, or slow or wrong results from a kernel meant for another chip.
check.attention_backend_dc_blackwell.example: A backend named after TensorRT-LLM kernels on an RTX 50 series card.

check.attention_backend_flashinfer_reuse.summary: The FlashInfer attention backend makes TensorRT-LLM switch off KV cache block reuse by itself.
check.attention_backend_flashinfer_reuse.details: Block reuse lets a new request skip text that an earlier request already processed. With the FlashInfer backend, TensorRT-LLM turns it off at start-up and only logs a note, so repeated prompts are recomputed every time. Your settings say block reuse is on, which no longer matches what the engine will do.
check.attention_backend_flashinfer_reuse.when_to_change: Set KV block reuse to off to match the engine, or switch the attention backend back to TRTLLM if you want prompts reused.

check.attention_backend_hopper_only.summary: The chosen attention backend targets Hopper (sm_90) and will not run on your card (sm_120).
check.attention_backend_hopper_only.details: Some attention backends use instructions that exist only on Hopper data-centre cards. On a workstation or consumer Blackwell card (compute capability 12.0) they cannot run, so the console blocks the launch before the engine crashes.
check.attention_backend_hopper_only.when_to_change: Choose flashinfer or triton, or leave the backend on auto.
check.attention_backend_hopper_only.risks: The engine would fail at start.
check.attention_backend_hopper_only.example: fa3 on an RTX PRO card.

check.attention_backend_vanilla.summary: The VANILLA attention backend is a slow reference version that NVIDIA does not recommend for production.
check.attention_backend_vanilla.details: VANILLA is a plain baseline for developers. It lacks the optimizations of the default TRTLLM kernels, so every step is slower.
check.attention_backend_vanilla.when_to_change: Switch the attention backend back to TRTLLM unless you are debugging attention behavior.

check.awq_gptq_sm120.summary: TensorRT-LLM does not list AWQ or GPTQ checkpoints as supported on RTX Blackwell (sm_120) cards.
check.awq_gptq_sm120.details: AWQ and GPTQ store weights in 4-bit formats made for other kernels. TensorRT-LLM's quantization table has no entry for them on sm_120, so loading can fail or fall back to slow code. FP8 and NVFP4 are listed for this card.
check.awq_gptq_sm120.when_to_change: Use an FP8 or NVFP4 build of the model, or run this model on vLLM or SGLang.

check.blackwell_cuda_build.summary: This is a Blackwell GPU and the engine image ships kernels built for it, so nothing needs changing.
check.blackwell_cuda_build.details: Blackwell cards need an engine built with GPU code for their compute capability. The console checked that this image's CUDA build includes it, so the engine can use the card at full speed.
check.blackwell_cuda_build.when_to_change: Nothing to do. If you pick a different image, the console checks it again.
check.blackwell_cuda_build.risks: None while this check is ok. An image without these kernels would fail to start or run much slower.
check.blackwell_cuda_build.example: A llama.cpp image built with CUDA 12.8 on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell card.

check.context_beyond_native.summary: The context length you set is longer than the model was trained for.
check.context_beyond_native.details: SGLang refuses a context longer than the model's native one unless the allow_longer_context_len setting is turned on, and the model should then get a rope-scaling method such as YaRN. The longer window also needs more KV cache.
check.context_beyond_native.when_to_change: Lower the context length to the model's native one, or turn on allow_longer_context_len and configure rope scaling together, then measure the quality and check the fit again.
check.context_beyond_native.risks: Start-up is refused, or answers get worse on long or short texts if you stretch the model too far.
check.context_beyond_native.example: A model trained for 32,768 tokens with a context of 131,072 requested.

check.cpu_offload_slow.summary: CPU offload keeps part of the weights in RAM and streams them to the GPU at every step, so expect a big slowdown.
check.cpu_offload_slow.details: With offload on, every token needs the offloaded weights to cross the PCIe link, which is far slower than reading VRAM. Offloading 10 GB can cut the speed to a fraction of what it was. It also uses host RAM.
check.cpu_offload_slow.when_to_change: Use it only when nothing else fits. Prefer a smaller or more compressed model, a shorter context, or more GPUs. If you must offload, offload as little as possible.
check.cpu_offload_slow.risks: Slow answers and high host RAM use.
check.cpu_offload_slow.example: cpu_offload_gb set to 10 on a model that is 10 GB too big for the card.

check.ctx_per_slot_small.summary: Sharing the context between slots leaves each conversation too few tokens.
check.ctx_per_slot_small.details: llama-server divides its context length evenly between its slots, one per parallel conversation. A 16,384-token context with 8 slots gives each conversation only 2,048 tokens, which long prompts exceed.
check.ctx_per_slot_small.when_to_change: Raise the context length, or lower the number of parallel slots.
check.ctx_per_slot_small.risks: Long prompts are cut off or refused.
check.ctx_per_slot_small.example: A context of 16,384 with 8 parallel slots: 2,048 tokens each.

check.cuda_graphs_off.summary: With CUDA graphs switched off, every decode step is noticeably slower.
check.cuda_graphs_off.details: CUDA graphs record the GPU's decode work once and replay it, which removes most of the per-step launch overhead. Turning them off is meant for debugging.
check.cuda_graphs_off.when_to_change: Turn CUDA graphs back on unless you are chasing a bug that graph recording hides.

check.deep_gemm_fp8_only.summary: The deep_gemm MoE backend only runs FP8 block-quantized models.
check.deep_gemm_fp8_only.details: DeepGEMM is a fast kernel library for mixture-of-experts layers, but it only handles weights quantized to FP8 in blocks. With any other weight format that backend cannot be used.
check.deep_gemm_fp8_only.when_to_change: Use an FP8 build of the model, or leave the MoE backend on auto.
check.deep_gemm_fp8_only.risks: Start-up fails, or vLLM picks another kernel than the one you asked for.
check.deep_gemm_fp8_only.example: moe_backend deep_gemm with an NVFP4 model.

check.default_context_by_vram.summary: With no context length set, Ollama picks a very large one on a big GPU and reserves memory for it.
check.default_context_by_vram.details: When no context length is given, Ollama chooses one from the free GPU memory, larger on bigger cards. It reserves KV cache for that whole context for every parallel request, which can take most of the card.
check.default_context_by_vram.when_to_change: Set the context length to what you need, for example 32,768 tokens.
check.default_context_by_vram.risks: The model takes far more memory than expected and leaves no room for other engines.
check.default_context_by_vram.example: No context length set on a 96 GB card.

check.dp_attention_dp_ne_tp.summary: Data-parallel attention needs the data-parallel size to equal the tensor-parallel size.
check.dp_attention_dp_ne_tp.details: In this mode the attention part is split by data parallelism over the same GPUs that tensor parallelism uses for the rest, so the two sizes must match. The console blocks other combinations.
check.dp_attention_dp_ne_tp.when_to_change: Set the data-parallel size to the tensor-parallel size, or turn data-parallel attention off.
check.dp_attention_dp_ne_tp.risks: The engine would refuse to start.
check.dp_attention_dp_ne_tp.example: tp_size 4 with dp_size 2 and DP attention on.

check.dp_attention_unsupported_arch.summary: Data-parallel attention is meant for DeepSeek-style and some Qwen mixture-of-experts models, and this one looks dense.
check.dp_attention_unsupported_arch.details: The mode helps models with a compressed (MLA) attention or a mixture-of-experts layout. For an ordinary dense model it brings little or nothing and may not be supported.
check.dp_attention_unsupported_arch.when_to_change: Turn it off for dense models.
check.dp_attention_unsupported_arch.risks: No gain, and possibly an error or slower start-up.
check.dp_attention_unsupported_arch.example: DP attention on a dense 8-billion-parameter model.

check.eager_slow.summary: Eager mode switches CUDA graphs off, which noticeably slows decoding.
check.eager_slow.details: Enforcing eager execution makes the engine launch every GPU operation separately. It saves the memory the graphs would use and helps debugging, but every token takes longer.
check.eager_slow.when_to_change: Leave it off, unless you are hunting a crash or are short of a little memory.
check.eager_slow.risks: Lower tokens per second, especially for small batches.
check.eager_slow.example: enforce_eager on a model that runs fine with graphs.

check.ep_dense_model.summary: Expert parallelism does nothing for a dense model.
check.ep_dense_model.details: Expert parallelism spreads the experts of a mixture-of-experts model over GPUs. A dense model has no experts, so the setting has no effect.
check.ep_dense_model.when_to_change: Turn it off, or choose a mixture-of-experts model.
check.ep_dense_model.risks: None, apart from a setting that suggests something that is not happening.

check.fit.summary: The summary of the memory estimate: fits, tight, won't fit or unknown, with its confidence.
check.fit.details: The level follows the verdict. Fits is ok, tight and unknown are warnings, and won't fit blocks the launch. When stopping a running engine would make room, the message says which one ('fits if you stop ...'). The launch form shows the full per-GPU breakdown.
check.fit.when_to_change: Open the memory meter for the breakdown. Then shorten the context, lower the concurrency or choose a smaller model until the verdict is fits.
check.fit.risks: A blocked fit stops the launch. A tight verdict risks failing at start or under load.

check.fit_auto_adjust.summary: llama-server sizes the context and the GPU layers you left unset to what fits the card.
check.fit_auto_adjust.details: Recent llama.cpp builds measure the free GPU memory at start-up and pick values for the settings you did not choose, such as the context length and how many layers go on the GPU. With that turned off, the engine allocates the model's full context, which can be far more than the card holds.
check.fit_auto_adjust.when_to_change: Leave it on unless you want exact, repeatable sizes; then set the context length and GPU layers yourself.
check.fit_auto_adjust.risks: With it off and nothing set, start-up can fail because the card runs out of memory.
check.fit_auto_adjust.example: A model with a 262,144-token native context started on a 32 GB card with no context length set.

check.fit_unavailable.summary: The console could not make a memory estimate for this launch, and the message says why.
check.fit_unavailable.details: The estimate needs a readable description of the model on that machine: its settings file with layers and heads. When the library scan has not seen it, or the model has none, there is no estimate. The launch is still allowed.
check.fit_unavailable.when_to_change: Rescan the library so the model's settings are read, then check again. If the model has no settings file, compare its size on disk with the card's memory yourself.
check.fit_unavailable.risks: Without an estimate nothing warns you before an out-of-memory failure.
check.fit_unavailable.example: A model folder copied without its config file.

check.format_unsupported.summary: This engine cannot load that kind of model file.
check.format_unsupported.details: Each engine reads certain model formats. For example, llama.cpp and Ollama read GGUF or their own store, while vLLM and SGLang read Hugging Face folders. The message lists the formats the engine does load.
check.format_unsupported.when_to_change: Choose an engine that loads this format, or pick the same model in a format this engine supports.
check.format_unsupported.example: A GGUF file offered to an engine that reads only Hugging Face folders.

check.fp8_block_scaling_sm120.summary: Block-scaled FP8 checkpoints are not listed as supported on RTX Blackwell (sm_120) cards by TensorRT-LLM.
check.fp8_block_scaling_sm120.details: Some FP8 checkpoints store a scale for every block of weights instead of one scale per tensor. TensorRT-LLM's hardware table lists FP8 per tensor for sm_120 but not block scaling, so the model may fail to load or run slowly.
check.fp8_block_scaling_sm120.when_to_change: Use an FP8 per-tensor build (for example one made with NVIDIA ModelOpt) or an NVFP4 build, or run the model on another engine.

check.fp8_recommended.summary: The unquantized weights nearly fill one GPU, and FP8 is the usual way to make room.
check.fp8_recommended.details: The model is stored at full precision and is over 90% of the smallest selected card's memory, which leaves almost nothing for the KV cache. Setting the quantization to fp8 halves the weights, or you can choose a ready-made FP8 or NVFP4 build.
check.fp8_recommended.when_to_change: Set quantization to fp8, or pick an FP8 or NVFP4 version of the model, or use more GPUs.
check.fp8_recommended.risks: The engine may fail to start for lack of memory, or leave only a tiny KV cache.
check.fp8_recommended.example: A 90 GB bf16 model on a 96 GB card.

check.gated_model.summary: The model is gated: accept its licence on Hugging Face and give the console a token.
check.gated_model.details: Gated models need permission before download. Until you accept the terms on the model's page with the account behind your token, the download fails with an access error.
check.gated_model.when_to_change: Accept the licence on the model's page and set your Hugging Face token in the console's settings.
check.gated_model.risks: The download fails or never starts.
check.gated_model.example: A model repository that shows 'You need to agree to share your contact information'.

check.gated_needs_hf_token.summary: The model is gated: set a Hugging Face token and accept the licence before downloading or starting it.
check.gated_needs_hf_token.details: Gated models need permission before download. The console downloads them with your token, so both the licence acceptance and the token must be in place.
check.gated_needs_hf_token.when_to_change: Accept the licence on the model's page and set your Hugging Face token in the settings.
check.gated_needs_hf_token.risks: The download fails with an access-denied message.
check.gated_needs_hf_token.example: A gated model with no token configured.

check.gateway_missing.summary: The machine's policy names no gateway image, so engines there cannot get their loopback gateway.
check.gateway_missing.details: Every engine is reached through a small gateway container on this machine. The image for it comes from the policy and must be an exact, allowed image that is already present. Without one, an engine would run but could not be reached, so the console blocks the launch.
check.gateway_missing.when_to_change: Ask the administrator to set the gateway image in the policy to a pinned nginx image that is on the machine.
check.gateway_missing.example: An older policy file written before gateways existed.

check.gpt_oss_prefer_ollama.summary: gpt-oss ships its own MXFP4 weights: leave quantization unset, and use llama.cpp or Ollama if vLLM does not start.
check.gpt_oss_prefer_ollama.details: gpt-oss models are published already compressed in the MXFP4 format, so forcing another quantization breaks the load. Whether vLLM runs them depends on the GPU generation; llama.cpp and Ollama are a reliable fallback.
check.gpt_oss_prefer_ollama.when_to_change: Leave quantization unset on vLLM. If vLLM does not start on your card, run the model with llama.cpp or Ollama instead.
check.gpt_oss_prefer_ollama.risks: A wrongly forced quantization makes the model misload.
check.gpt_oss_prefer_ollama.example: Choosing vLLM for a gpt-oss model.

check.gpu_shared.summary: Another engine already uses this GPU, so the launch relies on the memory that is free right now.
check.gpu_shared.details: Each engine reserves its share of a card when it starts. A second engine on the same card must fit in what the first one left. The estimate looks at the free memory at this moment, but the other engine can grow later, and a third program can take the rest.
check.gpu_shared.when_to_change: Choose a card that is not in use, lower this engine's memory share, or stop the other engine first.
check.gpu_shared.risks: The new engine may fail at start, or the one that was already there may run out of memory when this one loads.
check.gpu_shared.example: GPU already used by an engine with 60 GB: only the rest of the card is free.

check.gpu_unknown.summary: You selected a GPU number this machine does not have.
check.gpu_unknown.details: GPU numbers belong to one machine. The message lists the numbers that exist there. This can happen when you change the machine in the launch form but keep the GPU choice made for another one.
check.gpu_unknown.when_to_change: Pick from the GPUs listed for the chosen machine.
check.gpu_unknown.example: GPU 3 requested on a machine that has GPUs 0 and 1.

check.gpus_insufficient.summary: The settings need more GPUs than you selected.
check.gpus_insufficient.details: The tensor, pipeline and data parallel sizes multiply to the number of GPUs the engine needs (with data-parallel attention the data size is not multiplied). If that is more than the GPUs you selected, the launch cannot go ahead.
check.gpus_insufficient.when_to_change: Lower the parallel sizes or select more GPUs.
check.gpus_insufficient.risks: The engine would refuse to start.

check.gpus_unused.summary: More GPUs are selected than the parallel sizes use, so the extra ones stay reserved but idle.
check.gpus_unused.details: Tensor times pipeline times context parallel size decides how many GPUs one engine uses. The other selected GPUs are held for this launch, so other engines cannot use them, yet they do no work.
check.gpus_unused.when_to_change: Raise the tensor or pipeline parallel size to use them, or select fewer GPUs.

check.host_down.summary: The machine is not connected, so nothing can be started on it until its link is up.
check.host_down.details: The console starts engines through the machine's node. When the link is connecting, down, incompatible or disabled, it cannot ask for anything, and the other checks are skipped because they need facts from that machine. The message gives the reason the link is not up.
check.host_down.when_to_change: Open the host's page, read why the link is not up, fix that, and press Reconnect. Or choose another machine in the launch form.
check.host_down.risks: Nothing is launched. Instances already running there are not affected.
check.host_down.example: A machine that was powered off shows host_down.

check.hybrid_max_num_seqs.summary: Hybrid models need one cache block per running request, and the default request limit can be more than fits.
check.hybrid_max_num_seqs.details: Hybrid models mix attention layers with Mamba-style layers that keep a fixed-size state per request. vLLM needs one such block for every running request, and its default limit of 1024 requests on large cards can exceed what fits, which stops start-up during CUDA graph capture.
check.hybrid_max_num_seqs.when_to_change: Set max_num_seqs lower, for example 256, or raise gpu_memory_utilization.
check.hybrid_max_num_seqs.risks: Start-up stops with a message that max_num_seqs exceeds the available Mamba cache blocks.
check.hybrid_max_num_seqs.example: A hybrid model with the default max_num_seqs on a 96 GB card.

check.image_arch_unverified.summary: The pinned TensorRT-LLM image was only checked on x86-64 machines, and this machine has a different processor type.
check.image_arch_unverified.details: The console pinned an image that was inspected as an amd64 build. On an ARM machine the same tag may or may not carry a matching build.
check.image_arch_unverified.when_to_change: Set the image parameter to an arm64 build of the same release, and test the launch before relying on it.

check.image_check_failed.summary: The console could not find out whether the image is on the machine, and the message says why.
check.image_check_failed.details: It asked the machine's node whether the image is present, and the question failed or timed out, for example because Docker was not answering. The launch is still allowed, but it may fail later if the image is not there.
check.image_check_failed.when_to_change: Check that Docker works on that machine, then run the checks again.
check.image_check_failed.risks: If the image really is missing, the launch will fail after you press it instead of before.
check.image_check_failed.example: A Docker service that is restarting.

check.image_missing.summary: The engine image is not on the machine, and the console does not download it during a launch.
check.image_missing.details: GPU engine images are large, so the console leaves pulling them to you. Pull the image on that machine once, with its Docker, and the launch can go ahead. The message shows the exact reference.
check.image_missing.when_to_change: On that machine run docker pull with the image reference from the message, using the same Docker context the node uses. Then run the checks again.
check.image_missing.example: A newly installed machine that has never pulled an engine image.

check.image_not_allowed.summary: The engine image is not on this machine's list of allowed images.
check.image_not_allowed.details: Each machine's policy says which images may run on it, as exact references or as a repository followed by :*. The message names the image and the policy. This list is a safety limit chosen by the machine's administrator, so the console cannot override it.
check.image_not_allowed.when_to_change: Choose an image that is allowed, or ask the administrator to add yours to the engine images in the policy.
check.image_not_allowed.example: An engine image tag that is newer than the ones the policy lists.

check.image_pin_nemotron_omni.summary: The model card for this Nemotron Omni model asks for one exact vLLM version, and the chosen image is another.
check.image_pin_nemotron_omni.details: NVIDIA's model card names the single vLLM version that is known to load this model. Other versions may fail, which the console cannot verify. The rule is built in and can be outdated.
check.image_pin_nemotron_omni.when_to_change: Use the vLLM version the model card names, or test carefully with another one.
check.image_pin_nemotron_omni.risks: A failed load, or odd behaviour.
check.image_pin_nemotron_omni.example: A Nemotron 3 Nano Omni model with a newer vLLM than its card asks for.

check.image_version_unverified.summary: A different image than the pinned one may rename or remove settings.
check.image_version_unverified.details: The parameters and the engine options file were read from TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1. Other releases change option names, and the engine refuses names it does not know, so a launch that works here can stop at start-up.
check.image_version_unverified.when_to_change: Use the pinned image, or test this launch on the other image before relying on it.

check.insufficient_free_vram.summary: The memory share you set needs more GPU memory than is free on a card right now.
check.insufficient_free_vram.details: vLLM reserves memory share times the card's total at start. If less than that is free, because another engine or program holds some, the engine would stop at start with a memory error. The message says how much is free and suggests a lower share.
check.insufficient_free_vram.when_to_change: Stop the engine that holds the memory, or lower the memory share to fit what is free.
check.insufficient_free_vram.risks: The engine fails at start with an error about memory.
check.insufficient_free_vram.example: 0.9 on a 96 GB card needs about 86 GB free. With 40 GB used by another engine it fails.

check.invalid_launch.summary: The container description the console built was rejected by the same safety rules the node uses.
check.invalid_launch.details: Before sending a launch to a machine, the console checks the finished description (names, image, ports, mounts, shared-memory size and so on) against the rules the machine's node enforces. A violation stops the launch here instead of after a failed attempt. The message names the field.
check.invalid_launch.when_to_change: Read the message and change the value it names, for example a shared-memory size above the machine's limit. If the cause is the machine's policy, ask its administrator.
check.invalid_launch.example: A shared-memory size larger than the policy's maximum.

check.invalid_params.summary: One or more engine settings are not valid, and the message lists them by name.
check.invalid_params.details: A setting can be unknown, of the wrong type, outside its allowed range, missing from its list of choices, or in a combination the engine refuses, such as automatic tool choice without a tool-call parser. It also fires when a secret setting still shows the [set] placeholder instead of a real value, and when an image override is given as a setting, because the image is chosen in the launch form.
check.invalid_params.when_to_change: Read each message: it names the setting. Fix or clear it in the form. The form marks the fields.
check.invalid_params.risks: The engine would refuse to start or ignore the setting.
check.invalid_params.example: 'max_model_len: must be >= 1' names the setting and the rule.

check.iter_stats_off.summary: With iteration statistics switched off, the console has no live metrics for this engine.
check.iter_stats_off.details: TensorRT-LLM only reports running requests, queue length and KV cache use when iteration statistics are on. They are off in the engine by default; the console turns them on unless you switch them off.
check.iter_stats_off.when_to_change: Turn iteration statistics back on if you want the metrics page and the KV cache bar to work.

check.jinja_disabled.summary: With the Jinja template engine off, tool calls and reasoning output are not parsed.
check.jinja_disabled.details: Modern models describe their chat format in a Jinja chat template. llama-server needs that template engine to format tool calls and to separate a reasoning model's thinking from its answer. With it off, a simpler built-in format is used.
check.jinja_disabled.when_to_change: Keep Jinja on unless a model's template breaks; then fix the template rather than turning Jinja off.
check.jinja_disabled.risks: Tool calling does not work, and thinking text leaks into the answers.
check.jinja_disabled.example: Jinja turned off for a model that makes tool calls.

check.keep_alive_forever.summary: A negative keep-alive holds the model until the server stops, so other engines cannot use that memory.
check.keep_alive_forever.details: Ollama unloads a model after it has been idle for the keep-alive time. A negative value means never: the model stays in GPU memory even when nobody uses it.
check.keep_alive_forever.when_to_change: Use a time such as 30 minutes unless this machine serves only this model.
check.keep_alive_forever.risks: The GPU memory stays taken, so other models or engines cannot start.
check.keep_alive_forever.example: A keep-alive of -1 on a machine that also runs other engines.

check.kernel_backend_not_for_gpu.summary: The chosen MoE or linear kernel backend is not built for this GPU.
check.kernel_backend_not_for_gpu.details: Some kernel backends exist only for other chips: aiter and flydsl are for AMD GPUs, xpu is for Intel, and hpc is for FP8 on Hopper cards. They cannot run on this NVIDIA card.
check.kernel_backend_not_for_gpu.when_to_change: Use auto, cutlass, marlin or flashinfer_b12x.
check.kernel_backend_not_for_gpu.example: moe_backend aiter on an NVIDIA card.

check.kv_cache_fraction_high.summary: A KV cache share above 0.95 leaves too little free memory for buffers that grow later.
check.kv_cache_fraction_high.details: TensorRT-LLM gives the KV cache this share of the memory that is free after loading the model. What remains is the only margin for working memory that grows under load, so a very high share makes out of memory errors likely.
check.kv_cache_fraction_high.when_to_change: Use 0.9 or lower, and lower it further if another program shares the card.

check.kv_dtype_backend_mismatch.summary: The chosen attention backend cannot store the KV cache in the chosen data type.
check.kv_dtype_backend_mismatch.details: Each attention backend supports only some KV cache formats, and this combination is not one of them, so vLLM would stop at start-up. The message lists the formats this backend does support.
check.kv_dtype_backend_mismatch.when_to_change: Pick another attention backend or another KV cache dtype.
check.kv_dtype_backend_mismatch.example: An attention backend without fp8 support together with kv_cache_dtype fp8.

check.kv_exceeds_vram.summary: The conversation memory alone needs more than the free GPU memory.
check.kv_exceeds_vram.details: The KV cache for the chosen context length and number of parallel conversations is larger than the GPU memory left after the weights, so the card cannot hold that many tokens.
check.kv_exceeds_vram.when_to_change: Shorten the context, serve fewer conversations at once, use a compressed cache, or choose a GPU with more free memory.
check.kv_exceeds_vram.risks: Start-up fails with an out of memory error, or the engine keeps the cache in RAM and runs slowly.
check.kv_exceeds_vram.example: A 131,072-token context with 4 parallel conversations on a card with 10 GB free.

check.kv_fp4_experimental.summary: The FP4 KV cache is experimental, and its quality has not been validated here.
check.kv_fp4_experimental.details: Storing the KV cache in 4 bits cuts its size to a quarter, but the reduced precision can hurt answer quality in ways that depend on the model and the task.
check.kv_fp4_experimental.when_to_change: Prefer fp8 for the KV cache. If you use FP4, compare answers on your own prompts first.
check.kv_fp4_experimental.risks: Worse answers, especially in long conversations.

check.kv_fp8_accuracy.summary: An fp8 KV cache trades some accuracy for capacity, so check the answers on your own task.
check.kv_fp8_accuracy.details: Storing the KV cache in 8 bits doubles how many tokens fit, but the reduced precision can slightly change answers, and some models log a warning about it. The check appears when the model itself is not quantized.
check.kv_fp8_accuracy.when_to_change: Use it when the cache is the limit, and compare answers on your own prompts before relying on it.
check.kv_fp8_accuracy.risks: Small drops in quality, usually hard to notice, can appear in long conversations.
check.kv_fp8_accuracy.example: kv_cache_dtype fp8 on a bf16 model.

check.kv_fp8_flash_attn.summary: An fp8 KV cache does not work with the FLASH_ATTN backend on sm_120 cards, so vLLM refuses to start.
check.kv_fp8_flash_attn.details: On workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0) the FLASH_ATTN backend runs FlashAttention 2, which cannot read an fp8 KV cache, so vLLM stops at start-up. FLASHINFER can.
check.kv_fp8_flash_attn.when_to_change: Set the attention backend to FLASHINFER, or leave it unset, or set the KV cache dtype to auto.

check.kv_quant_needs_flash_attn.summary: A compressed conversation cache only works with flash attention on.
check.kv_quant_needs_flash_attn.details: Storing the KV cache in fewer bits, for example q8_0 or q4_0, saves memory, but llama.cpp and Ollama can only read such a cache through flash attention. Without it the engine refuses to start or ignores the setting.
check.kv_quant_needs_flash_attn.when_to_change: Turn flash attention on, or keep the cache type at its default f16.
check.kv_quant_needs_flash_attn.risks: Start-up fails, or the memory you expected to save is not saved.
check.kv_quant_needs_flash_attn.example: cache-type-k q8_0 with flash attention set to off.

check.linear_attn_flashinfer_needs_bf16_.summary: The FlashInfer linear-attention decode kernel needs the model's running state kept in bfloat16 on this GPU.
check.linear_attn_flashinfer_needs_bf16_.details: Some new models replace part of their attention with linear attention, which keeps a running state per request. On Blackwell cards SGLang's FlashInfer decode kernel for it only works when that state is stored in bfloat16, and SGLang stops at start-up otherwise.
check.linear_attn_flashinfer_needs_bf16_.when_to_change: Set mamba_ssm_dtype to bfloat16, or use the triton decode backend.

check.log_requests_leaks.summary: Request logging writes your prompts and the answers into the container's logs.
check.log_requests_leaks.details: With it on, every request is written to the log in full. Anyone who can read the logs, the console's log viewer included, can read your conversations.
check.log_requests_leaks.when_to_change: Leave it off, unless you are debugging and the data is not sensitive.
check.log_requests_leaks.risks: Private text stays in logs and backups for as long as they are kept.
check.log_requests_leaks.example: log_requests on an engine that serves private chats.

check.main_gpu_out_of_range.summary: The main GPU number is higher than the number of GPUs the engine can see.
check.main_gpu_out_of_range.details: The main GPU is counted from 0 among the GPUs given to this engine, not among all the GPUs in the machine. With two GPUs selected the valid values are 0 and 1.
check.main_gpu_out_of_range.when_to_change: Pick a number below the count of selected GPUs, or leave it unset.
check.main_gpu_out_of_range.example: Main GPU 2 with GPUs 0 and 1 selected.

check.max_len_exceeds_model.summary: The maximum model length is longer than the model was trained for, and no extension is set.
check.max_len_exceeds_model.details: vLLM refuses a context longer than the model's native one unless you extend it deliberately, with a YaRN override or the explicit long-length switch. Without that the engine stops at start-up.
check.max_len_exceeds_model.when_to_change: Lower the maximum model length, or set a YaRN override through the overrides setting, and check the fit again because a longer context needs more KV cache.
check.max_len_exceeds_model.risks: The engine would refuse to start.
check.max_len_exceeds_model.example: A model trained for 40,960 tokens with max_model_len 131072.

check.max_seq_len_capped.summary: The requested maximum length is above what TensorRT-LLM takes from the model's configuration, so the engine lowers it.
check.max_seq_len_capped.details: The engine reads the longest length from the model's own config, scaled by the rope setting for some types. A higher request is cut down without an error, and there is no option to extend a model's context. The server then refuses requests longer than the lowered limit.
check.max_seq_len_capped.when_to_change: Set the maximum length to the number in the message or lower. Use another engine if you need a longer context than the model config allows.

check.mem_fraction_high.summary: The memory share is above 92%, which leaves too little for CUDA graphs, prompt reading and scratch space.
check.mem_fraction_high.details: SGLang's static memory share covers the weights and the KV cache. The rest of the card must hold CUDA graphs, the buffers for reading prompts and scratch space. SGLang's own automatic choice keeps at least 10 GiB free on cards over 60 GB; above 92 % an out-of-memory error in the middle of a long prompt is likely.
check.mem_fraction_high.when_to_change: Keep it at 0.92 or lower, unless the card is dedicated to this engine and you tested it.
check.mem_fraction_high.risks: Out of memory under load, after the engine looked fine at start.
check.mem_fraction_high.example: 0.95 leaves 5% of a 96 GB card, about 4.8 GB.

check.metrics_forced.summary: Turning metrics off is ignored: the console needs the engine's metrics page.
check.metrics_forced.details: The console reads each engine's /metrics page for its dashboards and checks, so the console starts SGLang with metrics on whatever you set.
check.metrics_forced.when_to_change: Nothing to do. Leave the setting as it is.

check.mixed_chunk_needs_chunked_prefill.summary: Mixed chunks need chunked prefill, which a chunk size of -1 switches off.
check.mixed_chunk_needs_chunked_prefill.details: Mixed chunking puts pieces of a prompt and decoding steps into the same batch. That depends on chunked prefill, and a chunked prefill size of -1 turns it off, so the mix cannot work.
check.mixed_chunk_needs_chunked_prefill.when_to_change: Set a chunked prefill size greater than 0, or turn mixed chunking off.

check.mla_backend_arch.summary: The chosen MLA attention backend does not support sm_120 cards in this vLLM version.
check.mla_backend_arch.details: Models with latent attention need special kernels. In the pinned vLLM only TRITON_MLA, and FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 for sparse-MLA models, support compute capability 12.0; the others are built for data-centre cards. The console blocks them before the engine fails.
check.mla_backend_arch.when_to_change: Choose TRITON_MLA (or FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 for sparse-MLA models), or leave it unset.
check.mla_backend_arch.risks: The engine would fail at start.
check.mla_backend_arch.example: CUTLASS_MLA on an RTX PRO card.

check.model_missing.summary: The model is not in this machine's library, so the engine would not find it.
check.model_missing.details: An engine runs on one machine and can read only that machine's model folders (or storage it shares). The check looks at the library built from the machine's last scan. Models on other machines do not count, unless they sit on shared storage.
check.model_missing.when_to_change: Download the model to that machine, copy it from another machine's library, or rescan the library if you just added the files.
check.model_missing.example: A model that exists on the first machine but was never copied to the second.

check.modelopt_fp4_mismatch.summary: The modelopt_fp4 quantization needs an NVFP4 checkpoint made with ModelOpt.
check.modelopt_fp4_mismatch.details: This setting tells SGLang to expect weights that were already quantized to NVFP4 by NVIDIA's ModelOpt tool. If the checkpoint was quantized some other way, loading fails or produces wrong results.
check.modelopt_fp4_mismatch.when_to_change: Use a checkpoint that was made with ModelOpt in NVFP4, or unset the quantization setting.
check.modelopt_fp4_mismatch.risks: A load error or wrong results.

check.modelopt_unquantized.summary: ModelOpt quantization expects a pre-quantized checkpoint, and this model is not quantized.
check.modelopt_unquantized.details: ModelOpt settings read quantization data stored inside the checkpoint. A full-precision model has none, so the setting cannot work. For a bf16 model, FP8 quantization at load time is the simple route.
check.modelopt_unquantized.when_to_change: Use quantization fp8 for a bf16 model, or choose a checkpoint that was quantized with ModelOpt.

check.moe_backend_datacenter_only.summary: The chosen MoE backend is written for Hopper or data-centre Blackwell chips, not for RTX Blackwell cards.
check.moe_backend_datacenter_only.details: The DEEPGEMM, CUTEDSL, WIDEEP and TRITON backends check for sm_90, sm_100 or sm_103 in TensorRT-LLM's code, and nothing in the image says they run on sm_120. They may fail at start-up or run slowly.

check.moe_backend_triton_ep.summary: The TRITON MoE backend refuses expert parallelism on any GPU except Hopper.
check.moe_backend_triton_ep.details: TensorRT-LLM raises an error saying TritonFusedMoE is only supported on Hopper with an expert parallel size above 1. This card is not a Hopper GPU, so the engine stops at start-up.
check.moe_backend_triton_ep.when_to_change: Set the expert parallel size to 1 or use the CUTLASS backend.

check.moe_backend_trtllm_sm120.summary: The TRTLLM MoE backend raises an error on RTX Blackwell (sm_120) GPUs.
check.moe_backend_trtllm_sm120.details: TensorRT-LLM's code stops with the message that TRTLLMGenFusedMoE does not support SM120 and above when this backend is used on such a card, so the engine never finishes starting.
check.moe_backend_trtllm_sm120.when_to_change: Use the CUTLASS backend, which is the default.

check.moe_experts_on_cpu.summary: Expert weights stay in RAM, so RAM and its speed matter; on a dense model this setting does nothing.
check.moe_experts_on_cpu.details: In a mixture-of-experts model only a few experts work on each token. Keeping the experts in host RAM and the rest on the GPU lets a model far bigger than the card run at a usable speed, limited by memory bandwidth.
check.moe_experts_on_cpu.when_to_change: Use it when a MoE model does not fit in VRAM. On a dense model it has no effect.
check.moe_experts_on_cpu.risks: Slower than an all-GPU setup, and the experts take a lot of host RAM.
check.moe_experts_on_cpu.example: A 230-billion-parameter MoE model on a 96 GB card with its experts in RAM.

check.monitor_only.summary: The machine's node is in monitor mode: it can be watched but not changed, so nothing can be launched.
check.monitor_only.details: Monitor mode is the safe default. The message names the policy file and says what to change. The other checks still run, so you see every problem at once.
check.monitor_only.when_to_change: Ask the machine's administrator to set the mode to manage in its policy file, after reading what that allows. The console cannot change a policy. Or choose a machine that is in manage mode.
check.monitor_only.example: A freshly installed node is in monitor mode until its administrator changes it.

check.multimodal_block_reuse.summary: TensorRT-LLM's documentation says multimodal models do not work with KV cache block reuse.
check.multimodal_block_reuse.details: Models that accept images, video or audio need block reuse switched off in TensorRT-LLM. The documented example for them sets it to off.
check.multimodal_block_reuse.when_to_change: Turn KV block reuse off for this model.

check.mxfp4_family_unlisted.summary: TensorRT-LLM's support table lists MXFP4 only for gpt-oss, and this model is something else.
check.mxfp4_family_unlisted.details: MXFP4 is a 4-bit format. The table of supported models names only gpt-oss for it, so another MXFP4 model may not load.
check.mxfp4_family_unlisted.when_to_change: Use an FP8 or NVFP4 build of this model, or run it on another engine.

check.mxfp4_gptoss_engine.summary: gpt-oss models are validated with Ollama or llama.cpp; the SGLang route on sm_120 is unverified.
check.mxfp4_gptoss_engine.details: gpt-oss models are published in native MXFP4. The console's guidance, which may be out of date, is that Ollama and llama.cpp handle them on workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0) and that SGLang there has not been confirmed.
check.mxfp4_gptoss_engine.when_to_change: Try Ollama or llama.cpp first, or test SGLang on a small load before relying on it.
check.mxfp4_gptoss_engine.risks: A failed load or wrong results.
check.mxfp4_gptoss_engine.example: gpt-oss on SGLang on an RTX 50 series card.

check.mxfp4_moe_sm120.summary: MXFP4 mixture-of-experts models fail on sm_120 cards, except gpt-oss, so use an FP8 build.
check.mxfp4_moe_sm120.details: On workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0) the kernels for MXFP4 mixture-of-experts models stop at an assertion in the engine, with a single known exception, the gpt-oss models. The console blocks the launch instead of letting the engine crash.
check.mxfp4_moe_sm120.when_to_change: Use an FP8 version of the model, or quantize to fp8 at load time.
check.mxfp4_moe_sm120.risks: The engine would stop at start.
check.mxfp4_moe_sm120.example: An MXFP4 mixture-of-experts model other than gpt-oss on an RTX PRO card.

check.no_free_port.summary: Every port in this machine's range is taken, so there is none left for another engine.
check.no_free_port.details: Each engine instance needs a port in the range set by the machine's policy, for example 18000 to 18099. Stopped instances do not hold theirs. The message shows the range.
check.no_free_port.when_to_change: Remove instances you no longer need, or ask the machine's administrator to widen the port range in the policy.

check.no_gpu.summary: The machine reports no GPU, so no engine can run on it.
check.no_gpu.details: The node listed no graphics card. Typical causes are a driver that is not loaded, a missing container toolkit, or a machine without a GPU.
check.no_gpu.when_to_change: On that machine, check that the NVIDIA driver works (nvidia-smi lists the cards). Then reconnect the host.
check.no_gpu.example: A machine whose driver was removed by a kernel update.

check.no_tool_parser.summary: No tool-call parser is set for a model family that normally uses tools.
check.no_tool_parser.details: Without a parser, tool calls arrive as raw text in the reply and the standard tool-call field stays empty, so agent and coding tools stall. The check looks at the model's name for families known to use tools.
check.no_tool_parser.when_to_change: Set the tool-call parser that matches the model family if you serve tool-using clients. For plain chat you can ignore the warning.
check.no_tool_parser.risks: Agent clients appear to hang or loop.
check.no_tool_parser.example: A coding assistant that waits forever for a tool call.

check.nvfp4_kv_sm120.summary: An NVFP4 KV cache is not listed as supported on RTX Blackwell (sm_120) cards.
check.nvfp4_kv_sm120.details: An NVFP4 KV cache needs a checkpoint prepared for it, and TensorRT-LLM's hardware table has no entry for it on sm_120.
check.nvfp4_kv_sm120.when_to_change: Set the KV cache type to fp8 or auto.

check.nvfp4_moe_sm120.summary: NVFP4 mixture-of-experts models run on a slow kernel in vLLM on sm_120 cards.
check.nvfp4_moe_sm120.details: On workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0) vLLM uses a slow fallback kernel for NVFP4 mixture-of-experts models. The console's rule, which may be outdated for newer vLLM versions, advises an FP8 build, or SGLang.
check.nvfp4_moe_sm120.when_to_change: Use the FP8 version of the model, run it on SGLang, or test the MoE backend setting with cutlass, flashinfer_b12x or marlin.
check.nvfp4_moe_sm120.risks: It runs, but much slower than the card can go.
check.nvfp4_moe_sm120.example: An NVFP4 mixture-of-experts model on vLLM with an RTX 50 series card.

check.nvfp4_ok_sglang.summary: NVFP4 is supported here; for mixture-of-experts models SGLang is the recommended engine on sm_120.
check.nvfp4_ok_sglang.details: An information line. NVFP4 dense models are supported on workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0). For NVFP4 mixture-of-experts models, SGLang is the engine the console recommends, because vLLM falls back to a slow path there.
check.nvfp4_ok_sglang.example: An NVFP4 mixture-of-experts model on SGLang.

check.parallel_multiplies_context.summary: Ollama multiplies the context by the number of parallel requests, so memory grows with it.
check.parallel_multiplies_context.details: Each parallel request gets its own full context. With 4 parallel requests and an 8,192-token context, Ollama reserves KV cache for 32,768 tokens.
check.parallel_multiplies_context.when_to_change: Lower the parallel requests or the context when memory is tight.
check.parallel_multiplies_context.risks: More memory is used than you expect, and the model may spill partly to the CPU and slow down.
check.parallel_multiplies_context.example: 4 parallel requests with a context of 8,192 reserve space for 32,768 tokens.

check.port.summary: The loopback port the console picked for this engine's gateway.
check.port.details: An information line. The console takes the first free port in the machine's range, skipping ports that another instance or any container already publishes. You reach the engine at that port on that machine.

check.port_in_use.summary: The port the console chose is already taken by another program on the machine.
check.port_in_use.details: Normally the console moves on to the next free port by itself. You only see this when the ports it tried were all taken at the same moment, or something else grabbed the port between the check and the start.
check.port_in_use.when_to_change: Try again. If it repeats, find what uses the ports of the range, or widen the range in the policy.
check.port_in_use.example: A program started by hand on port 18000.

check.pp_with_speculation.summary: MTP and EAGLE-3 speculation do not work together with pipeline parallelism.
check.pp_with_speculation.details: TensorRT-LLM's feature table says No for these combinations, so the engine can fail or ignore the speculation.
check.pp_with_speculation.when_to_change: Use tensor parallelism instead, or turn speculation off.

check.prefix_hash_xxhash_missing.summary: The xxhash prefix-cache hash needs a package that this vLLM image does not include.
check.prefix_hash_xxhash_missing.details: Prefix caching recognises repeated prompt beginnings by hashing them. The xxhash option is faster, but it needs the optional xxhash package, which the pinned vLLM image lacks, so start-up fails unless your image adds it.
check.prefix_hash_xxhash_missing.when_to_change: Keep the default sha256, or use sha256_cbor.
check.prefix_hash_xxhash_missing.example: prefix_caching_hash_algo xxhash on the stock image.

check.quant_format_unlisted.summary: The checkpoint's quantization format is not among the recipes TensorRT-LLM documents.
check.quant_format_unlisted.details: TensorRT-LLM documents FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ and GPTQ recipes. Other formats such as bitsandbytes or GGUF are not listed, so the model may not load.
check.quant_format_unlisted.when_to_change: Use a BF16, FP8 or NVFP4 build of the model.

check.quant_override_prequantized.summary: You forced a quantization on a model that is already quantized, and it will load wrongly.
check.quant_override_prequantized.details: A pre-quantized checkpoint (AWQ, GPTQ, FP8, NVFP4 and so on) carries its own quantization settings, and the engine reads them. Forcing a different method on top misloads it. The console treats this as an error on vLLM and as a warning on SGLang.
check.quant_override_prequantized.when_to_change: Unset the quantization setting and let the engine detect it.
check.quant_override_prequantized.risks: A failed load, or garbled answers.
check.quant_override_prequantized.example: quantization fp8 on an AWQ checkpoint.

check.reasoning_parser_mismatch.summary: The reasoning parser setting does not suit this model family, or one is missing.
check.reasoning_parser_mismatch.details: Reasoning models write their thinking before the answer, and the reasoning parser separates the two. A parser for another family splits at the wrong place, and without one the thinking stays in the answer text.
check.reasoning_parser_mismatch.when_to_change: Set the reasoning parser that the message names.

check.reasoning_parser_missing.summary: This model family writes out its reasoning, but no reasoning parser is set, so the thinking leaks into the answer.
check.reasoning_parser_missing.details: Reasoning models put their chain of thought in the reply text. A reasoning parser separates it from the final answer. Without it, clients see a long block of thinking in front of the answer, and tools that expect a clean reply can break.
check.reasoning_parser_missing.when_to_change: Set the reasoning parser the message names, if you want the thinking shown separately or removed.
check.reasoning_parser_missing.example: A reasoning model answering with a page of thinking first.

check.secret_in_argv.summary: A secret setting would end up on the container's command line, where other users on the machine could read it.
check.secret_in_argv.details: Some engines accept their API key only as a command-line argument. Anyone who can list processes or inspect the container could read it. The console refuses to build such a launch.
check.secret_in_argv.when_to_change: Unset the secret setting, or use an engine that reads it from an environment variable. Put access control in front of the engine instead.
check.secret_in_argv.risks: A key on a command line leaks to every local user and appears in process listings and in logs.
check.secret_in_argv.example: An api_key setting on an engine that has no environment variable for it.

check.sleep_mode_dev_router.summary: Sleep mode's control endpoints need vLLM's developer mode, which the console never turns on.
check.sleep_mode_dev_router.details: Sleep mode lets an engine release GPU memory without exiting. Its control endpoints exist only in a developer mode that also opens an unauthenticated remote-call endpoint, so the console does not switch it on and the feature cannot be used through it.
check.sleep_mode_dev_router.when_to_change: Do not rely on sleep mode here. Stop and start the instance, or use the idle timeout.
check.sleep_mode_dev_router.risks: The setting is accepted, but the sleep controls do not work.

check.spec_type_needs_model.summary: This speculative decoding type needs a draft model file or a model with built-in prediction layers.
check.spec_type_needs_model.details: Speculative decoding guesses several tokens ahead with something cheap and lets the main model check the guesses. The type you chose takes its guesses from a draft model, or from the extra MTP layers some models ship, and neither is set or present.
check.spec_type_needs_model.when_to_change: Give a draft model file, choose a type that needs none, or turn speculative decoding off.
check.spec_type_needs_model.risks: Start-up fails, or the setting has no effect.
check.spec_type_needs_model.example: A draft-model speculative type with no draft model file given.

check.split_mode_none_multi_gpu.summary: The single-GPU split mode uses one card, so the other selected GPUs stay idle.
check.split_mode_none_multi_gpu.details: With split mode none, llama.cpp puts the whole model on its main GPU. Any other GPUs you selected are reserved for this engine but do no work.
check.split_mode_none_multi_gpu.when_to_change: Select a single GPU, or use the layer split mode to spread the model across all of them.
check.split_mode_none_multi_gpu.risks: Wasted GPUs, and the model may not fit on one card.
check.split_mode_none_multi_gpu.example: Split mode none with two GPUs selected.

check.split_mode_tensor_experimental.summary: The tensor split mode is experimental and needs flash attention.
check.split_mode_tensor_experimental.details: In tensor mode every layer is cut across the GPUs, like tensor parallelism in other engines. In this llama.cpp build it is marked experimental and only works with flash attention on.
check.split_mode_tensor_experimental.when_to_change: Prefer the layer split mode unless you are testing. If you use tensor mode, turn flash attention on.
check.split_mode_tensor_experimental.risks: Start-up fails, or the engine is slower or less stable than with the layer split.
check.split_mode_tensor_experimental.example: Split mode tensor across two GPUs with flash attention off.

check.tensor_split_mismatch.summary: The GPU split lists more GPUs than this engine has been given.
check.tensor_split_mismatch.details: The tensor split says what share of the model goes on each GPU, one number per GPU. It has more numbers than the GPUs selected for this engine, so the extra shares point at cards it cannot use.
check.tensor_split_mismatch.when_to_change: Give one number per selected GPU, or select more GPUs.
check.tensor_split_mismatch.risks: The engine may refuse to start, or place the model differently than you meant.
check.tensor_split_mismatch.example: A split of 3,1 with only one GPU selected.

check.tool_parser_dialect_mismatch.summary: The tool-call parser does not match this model family's tool format.
check.tool_parser_dialect_mismatch.details: Each model family writes tool calls in its own style. A parser for another style fails to find the calls, so tool-using clients get nothing. The message names the parser that fits the model.
check.tool_parser_dialect_mismatch.when_to_change: Use the parser the message recommends.
check.tool_parser_dialect_mismatch.risks: Tools are silently ignored or fail.
check.tool_parser_dialect_mismatch.example: A parser for JSON tool calls on a model that writes XML-style calls.

check.tool_parser_inactive.summary: A tool-call parser is set, but automatic tool choice is off, so the parser does nothing.
check.tool_parser_inactive.details: The parser only runs when the engine is allowed to choose tools by itself. Without that switch the setting has no effect.
check.tool_parser_inactive.when_to_change: Turn on automatic tool choice, or clear the parser.
check.tool_parser_inactive.risks: Tool calls arrive as raw text.

check.tool_parser_mismatch.summary: The tool-call parser setting does not match this model family's format, or one is missing.
check.tool_parser_mismatch.details: Models write tool calls in family-specific text. TensorRT-LLM ships six parsers. A parser for another family lets raw tool markup leak into the answer, and without one the calls come back as plain text.
check.tool_parser_mismatch.when_to_change: Set the tool parser that the message names.

check.tool_parser_missing.summary: No tool-call parser is set for a model family that uses tools, so agent and tool use will not work.
check.tool_parser_missing.details: The console recognised the model family and knows which parser it needs. Without one, tool calls come back as raw text and the tool-call field of the reply stays empty. The message gives the parser to set, and the switch for automatic tool choice.
check.tool_parser_missing.when_to_change: If you serve agents or coding tools, turn on automatic tool choice and set the parser the message names.
check.tool_parser_missing.example: A Qwen coder model with no parser.

check.torch_compile_slow_start.summary: torch.compile is experimental here and adds minutes to the start.
check.torch_compile_slow_start.details: The compiler builds optimised code for your model and GPU. The first start spends minutes on it, and later starts reuse the cached result. The feature is marked experimental in this engine.
check.torch_compile_slow_start.when_to_change: Leave it off unless you have measured a gain for your model.
check.torch_compile_slow_start.risks: A long start, and possibly crashes or hangs.

check.tp_exceeds_gpus.summary: The tensor, pipeline and data parallel sizes together need more GPUs than you selected.
check.tp_exceeds_gpus.details: Their product is the number of GPUs the engine needs. If it is larger than the number you selected, the launch cannot go ahead.
check.tp_exceeds_gpus.when_to_change: Lower the parallel sizes or select more GPUs.
check.tp_exceeds_gpus.risks: The engine would refuse to start.

check.tp_heads_indivisible.summary: The model's attention heads cannot be split evenly across the tensor-parallel size.
check.tp_heads_indivisible.details: Tensor parallelism gives each GPU the same number of attention heads. A model with 40 heads can go on 2, 4, 5, 8 GPUs but not on 3 or 6. The console blocks sizes that do not divide the head count.
check.tp_heads_indivisible.when_to_change: Pick a tensor-parallel size that divides the model's number of attention heads.
check.tp_heads_indivisible.risks: The engine would refuse to start.

check.tp_kv_heads_indivisible.summary: The model's key-value heads and the tensor-parallel size do not fit together: one must divide the other.
check.tp_kv_heads_indivisible.details: With grouped-query attention the model has fewer key-value heads than query heads. For each GPU to get a whole number of them, either the heads divide evenly across the GPUs, or the GPUs divide evenly across the heads, in which case some are copied.
check.tp_kv_heads_indivisible.when_to_change: Choose a tensor-parallel size that divides the number of key-value heads or is divided by it.
check.tp_kv_heads_indivisible.risks: The engine would refuse to start.

check.tp_memory_unbalanced.summary: The selected GPUs have very different amounts of free memory, which SGLang refuses for tensor parallelism.
check.tp_memory_unbalanced.details: With tensor parallelism every card holds an equal share of the model, so SGLang checks that the free memory on the cards differs by at most 10 % and stops with 'The memory capacity is unbalanced' otherwise.
check.tp_memory_unbalanced.when_to_change: Free memory on the busier card, stop what shares it, or choose cards with similar free memory.
check.tp_memory_unbalanced.example: One card with 90 GB free and one with 30 GB free.

check.tp_over_pcie.summary: Splitting a model across several GPUs makes them exchange data after every layer, which is slow over PCIe.
check.tp_over_pcie.details: The console warns whenever tensor parallelism is used, without checking the hardware. Without NVLink the cards exchange partial results over the PCIe bus after every layer, which costs speed. With NVLink it costs much less.
check.tp_over_pcie.when_to_change: If the model fits on one card, run one engine per card instead. Use tensor parallelism only when the model needs more memory than one card has.
check.tp_over_pcie.risks: Speed below what the number of cards suggests.
check.tp_over_pcie.example: A model that fits on one card, run on two with tensor parallelism, is often slower per request.

check.trtllm_mha_fp8_kv_sm120.summary: The trtllm_mha prefill kernel cannot use an fp8 KV cache on sm_120 cards.
check.trtllm_mha_fp8_kv_sm120.details: On workstation and consumer Blackwell cards (compute capability 12.0) SGLang's trtllm_mha prefill attention kernel does not support an fp8_e4m3 KV cache, and SGLang stops at start-up.
check.trtllm_mha_fp8_kv_sm120.when_to_change: Use kv_cache_dtype auto, or another prefill attention backend such as flashinfer.

check.trtllm_sampler_conflict.summary: The TRTLLMSampler cannot be combined with MTP or EAGLE-3 speculation.
check.trtllm_sampler_conflict.details: TensorRT-LLM stops at start-up with a message that the two are not supported together.
check.trtllm_sampler_conflict.when_to_change: Set the sampler type to auto.

check.trust_remote_code.summary: A setting lets the engine run Python code taken from the model's repository.
check.trust_remote_code.details: Some new model designs ship their own code. Allowing it means that code runs inside the engine's container with whatever the container can read, such as your prompts. The container has no internet access, which limits the damage, but it is still code you did not write. It is off unless you set it.
check.trust_remote_code.when_to_change: Leave it off unless the model needs it, and read the repository's code before you allow it.
check.trust_remote_code.risks: Hostile code could read prompts and mounted files, or use the GPU for something else.
check.trust_remote_code.example: A model repository that contains its own .py files.

check.unsupported_architecture.summary: TensorRT-LLM's PyTorch backend has no model class for this model's architecture.
check.unsupported_architecture.details: The backend registers 50 architectures and raises an Unknown architecture error for any other, so the engine stops while loading.
check.unsupported_architecture.when_to_change: Run the model on vLLM or SGLang, or choose a supported family such as Llama, Qwen3, Mistral or gpt-oss.

check.util_very_high.summary: The memory share is above 95%, which leaves little room for CUDA graphs and activation spikes.
check.util_very_high.details: vLLM reserves this share of the card at start for the weights and the KV cache. The rest has to hold CUDA graphs and temporary buffers. With less than 5% left, an out-of-memory error at start is likely.
check.util_very_high.when_to_change: Use 0.90 to 0.92, unless the card is dedicated to this engine and you tested it.
check.util_very_high.example: 0.97 on a 96 GB card leaves about 2.9 GB.

check.weights_exceed_gpu.summary: The model's weights are bigger than one card's memory, and TensorRT-LLM loads checkpoints as they are.
check.weights_exceed_gpu.details: The PyTorch backend ignores quantization settings, so a 16-bit checkpoint stays 16-bit. Each GPU must hold its share of the weights, plus memory for the KV cache and working buffers.
check.weights_exceed_gpu.when_to_change: Pick an FP8 or NVFP4 checkpoint, or spread the model over more GPUs.

check.weights_prefetch_host_ram.summary: Start-up reads the whole checkpoint into the machine's RAM, which briefly needs about as much free memory as the checkpoint.
check.weights_prefetch_host_ram.details: TensorRT-LLM reads checkpoint files into host memory before loading them to the GPU, up to 16 files at once for each GPU worker. It skips this read-ahead when the files are larger than 90 percent of the free RAM. In between, other programs can be starved of memory for a short time.
check.weights_prefetch_host_ram.when_to_change: Stop memory-heavy programs before starting this engine.

check.world_exceeds_gpus.summary: Tensor, pipeline and context parallel sizes multiplied need more GPUs than are selected.
check.world_exceeds_gpus.details: One engine uses tensor times pipeline times context parallel size GPUs. With fewer GPUs selected it cannot start.
check.world_exceeds_gpus.when_to_change: Lower the sizes or select more GPUs.

check.yarn_short_context_quality.summary: The context was stretched past the trained length with a static YaRN override, so short prompts can lose quality.
check.yarn_short_context_quality.details: A static YaRN override rescales every position, so it also affects short texts, not just long ones. The quality loss can be small or noticeable, and depends on the model. Measure it before you adopt it.
check.yarn_short_context_quality.when_to_change: Test on your own prompts, both short and long. If short prompts get worse, use a shorter context without the override for them.
check.yarn_short_context_quality.risks: Slightly worse answers on short texts.
check.yarn_short_context_quality.example: A model trained for 32,768 tokens running at 131,072 with YaRN.

confidence.high.summary: All the facts the estimate needs were known, so the number is as good as this method gets.
confidence.high.details: The model's layers, heads and sizes were read, the weights size is known from the files, and no rule had to guess. High confidence describes the inputs, not the outcome: the method itself has not been calibrated against real launches.
confidence.high.risks: Even at high confidence the result is an estimate.
confidence.high.example: A standard model with a full settings file and safetensors sizes gives high confidence.

confidence.low.summary: Key facts were missing, so the number is a rough guide at best.
confidence.low.details: The layers, heads or head size needed to size the KV cache, or the weights size, were missing. The estimator degrades instead of inventing numbers. At low confidence the verdict is often 'unknown'.
confidence.low.when_to_change: Do not rely on it. Check the model's settings file, rescan the library, or launch with small settings and measure.
confidence.low.risks: Any verdict at low confidence can be wrong in either direction.
confidence.low.example: A model folder with a partial config gives low confidence.

confidence.medium.summary: Some inputs were worked out or assumed, so expect a wider margin of error.
confidence.medium.details: Examples: the weights size was derived from the parameter count instead of the file sizes, the model's native context length is unknown, the working-buffer size had to be guessed, or an assumption was made about layers that look back only a short way.
confidence.medium.when_to_change: Treat a 'fits' with medium confidence as probably fine, and a 'tight' as risky. Rescan the library or check the model's settings if you can.
confidence.medium.risks: The real memory use may differ from the estimate by more than usual.
confidence.medium.example: A quantized model whose file sizes were not available gives medium confidence.

config.env.allowed_hosts.summary: Extra Host header values the console accepts, a JSON list set as ENGINE_CONSOLE_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
config.env.allowed_hosts.details: Default empty. The console always accepts localhost, the loopback addresses and its bind address, each with its port, and refuses any other Host header, which blocks web pages that try to reach it through a changed DNS name. Entries are compared exactly, upper and lower case alike. The bare name ALLOWED_HOSTS is ignored.
config.env.allowed_hosts.when_to_change: Add the name your reverse proxy forwards, when the console sits behind one with its own hostname. The console reads it only when it starts: restart the console to apply a change.
config.env.allowed_hosts.risks: A missing entry makes every request through the proxy fail. Adding names you do not control weakens that protection. A value that is not a JSON list stops the start.

config.env.background_tasks.summary: Whether the console runs its background loops: the supervisor and the metrics collection, set as BACKGROUND_TASKS.
config.env.background_tasks.details: true or false; default true. The supervisor follows starting engines, checks health, stops idle ones and adopts containers when a machine connects. The metrics loop gathers the engines' numbers. Off is for tests.
config.env.background_tasks.risks: Off, engines never turn ready on the page, idle timeouts never fire and charts stay empty.
config.env.background_tasks.example: BACKGROUND_TASKS=false is what the test suites use.

config.env.body_cap_bytes.summary: The largest request body, in bytes, the console accepts on most API calls, set as BODY_CAP_BYTES.
config.env.body_cap_bytes.details: Default 1048576 (1 MiB). Chat and profile import have their own limits. A larger body is refused with 413.
config.env.body_cap_bytes.when_to_change: Leave it alone: normal requests are a few kilobytes. The console reads it only when it starts: restart the console to apply a change.
config.env.body_cap_bytes.risks: Too low and ordinary forms fail with 413. A negative number becomes 0, which refuses every request with a body.
config.env.body_cap_bytes.example: 1048576 allows a 1 MiB request, far more than a launch form needs.

config.env.chat_body_cap_bytes.summary: The largest chat request, in bytes, the console accepts, set as CHAT_BODY_CAP_BYTES.
config.env.chat_body_cap_bytes.details: Default 33554432 (32 MiB), for POST /api/v1/chat/completions only, so that long conversations and attached images fit. A larger body is refused with 413.
config.env.chat_body_cap_bytes.when_to_change: Raise it only if chats with large images are refused with 413. The console reads it only when it starts: restart the console to apply a change.
config.env.chat_body_cap_bytes.risks: Too low and long chats or image chats fail. Very high lets one request hold a lot of the hub's memory.

config.env.data_dir.summary: The folder that holds the console's database, engine secrets and first-start admin key, set as ENGINE_CONSOLE_DATA_DIR.
config.env.data_dir.details: Default ~/.local/share/engine-console. It holds console.db (API keys as hashes, instances, history, library snapshots), secrets/ (engine secret parameters, mode 0600), bootstrap-admin.key after the first start and the desktop launcher's log, pid and lock files. The bare name DATA_DIR is ignored.
config.env.data_dir.when_to_change: Change it only to move all of the console's state, for example to a backed-up disk: stop the console, move the folder, set the variable, start the console.
config.env.data_dir.risks: An empty folder starts a fresh console: no instances, no history and no keys, so a new bootstrap admin key is written. Its contents are sensitive: keep the folder private to your user and in your backups.
config.env.data_dir.example: ENGINE_CONSOLE_DATA_DIR=/srv/engine-console keeps the database outside the home folder.

config.env.discovery_enabled.summary: An old switch for the hub's own engine discovery that no longer does anything, set as DISCOVERY_ENABLED.
config.env.discovery_enabled.details: Each node now finds the engines it did not start, from its containers and from the ports in its policy's discovery_ports. The value still parses but nothing reads it. Default true.
config.env.discovery_enabled.when_to_change: Leave it unset. To stop a machine probing ports, set discovery_ports to [] in its node policy.
config.env.discovery_enabled.risks: Nothing breaks if it is set, but setting it to false does not stop any probing.

config.env.discovery_interval_s.summary: An old setting for how often the hub looked for engines; it no longer does anything, set as DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_S.
config.env.discovery_interval_s.details: Discovery now happens on each node, from its own inventory rounds. The value still parses but nothing reads it. Default 10 seconds.
config.env.discovery_interval_s.risks: Nothing breaks if it is set, but changing it changes nothing.

config.env.discovery_ports.summary: An old list of ports the hub probed for engines; it no longer does anything, set as DISCOVERY_PORTS.
config.env.discovery_ports.details: Each node now probes the ports in its own policy's discovery_ports. The value still parses (a JSON list of numbers) but nothing reads it. Default 8000, 30000, 11434, 8001 and 18000 to 18099.
config.env.discovery_ports.when_to_change: Leave it unset and set discovery_ports in each machine's node policy.
config.env.discovery_ports.risks: Nothing breaks if it is set, but the ports it names are not probed.
config.env.discovery_ports.example: DISCOVERY_PORTS=[8000] has no effect; "discovery_ports": [8000] in the policy does.

config.env.docker_bin.summary: An old setting for the docker program the hub runs; it no longer does anything, set as DOCKER_BIN.
config.env.docker_bin.details: The hub runs no docker commands itself: each machine's node does, with the program named in its policy's docker.binary. The value still parses, so an old env file keeps working, but nothing reads it. Default docker.
config.env.docker_bin.when_to_change: Leave it unset. For a docker outside the standard folders, set docker.binary in that machine's node policy.
config.env.docker_bin.risks: Nothing breaks if it is set, but changing it changes nothing: docker.binary in the policy is the setting that counts.

config.env.docker_context.summary: The docker context name the console shows, and in the real environment a fallback for its own machine's node, set as DOCKER_CONTEXT.
config.env.docker_context.details: Default rootless. The setting itself is only echoed by GET /settings and /health; nodes use their policy's docker.context. Separately, a DOCKER_CONTEXT variable in the console's real environment (not the env file) is passed on to the local node, which uses it only when its policy names no context. Remote nodes never get it.
config.env.docker_context.when_to_change: Leave it alone. Name the context in each machine's node policy (docker.context) instead.
